passage: Section 2.4 (taxonomy), [L1.2] Pre-processing on training and test set: the entire dataset is used for pre-processing steps 'such as imputation or over/under sampling' (the quoted fragment is the part of the entry that names the steps; the entry's example is oversampling). PB section 1 O-1 extends L1.2 to pre-processing that does not use the labels (scaling, unsupervised imputation, PCA on all data); that extension is PB's, not KAP23's wording.
faulty: Standardise the markers and compute the principal component projection (first 10 components) once on all patients, then run 5-fold cross-validation of the linear regression of outcome on those 10 component scores. The test fold's rows have therefore contributed to the centring, scaling and component directions. Parameters: 10 components, 5 folds (no further parameters documented by KAP23).
fixed: Inside each of the 5 folds, fit the standardisation and the principal components on the training rows only, project the test rows with them, fit the regression on the training scores, predict the test rows; R-squared over the pooled out-of-fold predictions.
estimand: Faulty: cross-validated R-squared of outcome on 10 principal components whose basis was computed from all rows, test rows included. Fixed: out-of-sample R-squared of the whole pipeline (standardisation, components, regression) for new patients, estimated by 5-fold cross-validation with all steps fitted inside the training folds. The claim names principal components because the estimand (the pipeline's predictive R-squared) requires them.
guard_minimum: 15 patients (5 folds, at least 3 rows per test fold and at least 11 training rows for 10 components plus intercept); also non-finite values and zero variance of outcome return None
sizes_note: KAP23 states no sample sizes for this entry. 300 patients x 80 markers (24 000 values) is realistic for a biomarker panel cohort and far inside the timing rule: a 5-fold SVD of 240x80 takes about a millisecond, so t+g is well below 0.05 s and the estimate 2*200*(S+1)*(t+g) stays under a minute. KAP23 reports nothing on how the size of this error depends on sample size or number of features: not stated (the effect of unsupervised pre-processing on all rows is generally small and shrinks with n, but that is my knowledge, not the source's).
notes: KAP23 labels: L1.2, class O-1 (pre-processing that does not use the outcome labels). Distinct from O1-B in the pipeline step (pre-processing vs evaluation sample) and statistic family.

passage: Section 2.4 (taxonomy), [L3.3] Sampling bias in test distribution; the entry's selection-bias example cites Bone et al. (2015) on autism: 'excluding the data corresponding to borderline cases of autism leads to leakage' (short quote as returned by my reading tool; entry located by section).
faulty: Compute the cross-validated balanced accuracy of a logistic regression of diagnosis on the speech measures only on children whose severity rating is clearly low or clearly high: children whose rating falls in the middle 30 percent of the rating distribution (between the 35th and 65th percentile) are dropped before cross-validation, so the borderline children are never evaluated. KAP23 documents the practice (borderline cases excluded) but no percentage; the 30 percent band is my choice and is stated as such.
fixed: Cross-validated (5-fold, stratified by diagnosis) balanced accuracy of the same logistic regression on all children, borderline ones included.
estimand: Faulty: balanced accuracy for new children whose severity rating lies outside the middle band. Fixed: balanced accuracy for new children referred for assessment, i.e. the whole referred population the claim is about. The claim names the population ('children referred for a developmental assessment') because the estimand requires it; the rating key is a measured quantity of the cohort.
guard_minimum: 10 children with at least 2 of each diagnosis value (so that each class is present in training and test folds of a 5-fold evaluation); non-finite values return None
sizes_note: KAP23 and Bone et al. as read give no sample size for this entry. 400 children x 30 measures (12 000 values) is a realistic clinic-cohort size and fits the timing rule easily (5-fold logistic regression on 400x30 in a few ms with a fixed number of Newton steps, estimate well under 15 minutes). The source reports nothing on how the size of this error depends on sample size or number of features: not stated.
notes: KAP23 label L3.3, class O-1. The 'severity_rating' key is named by what it measures (a clinician's rating), not by its role; risk that an auditor reads it as role-naming is logged in LOG.md. The faulty criterion needs a quantity by which borderline cases can be recognised; the claim does not mention it.

passage: Table 1 note and text, Situation A: 'Results for Situation A were obtained by conducting three t tests, one on each of two dependent variables and a third on the average of these two variables.' Simulated false-positive rate at p < .05 is 9.5% (two dependent variables, r = .50, 20 observations per cell, 15,000 simulations).
faulty: Run three two-sample t tests (equal variances): on liking, on willingness to pay, and on the average of the two (each variable standardised is not documented; use the raw average of the two measures as in the source's wording 'the average of these two variables'). Report the claim as holding if any of the three has a positive mean difference and p < .05. Parameters: 20 participants per cell, two measures, alpha .05, three tests.
fixed: One two-sample t test (equal variances) on liking only, the single measure the claim names, at p < .05 with a positive mean difference.
estimand: Faulty: whether at least one of three treatment-control comparisons (liking, willingness to pay, their average) is significant. Fixed: the treatment-minus-control difference in mean liking. The claim names only liking; the data keys name the second measure because the keys list what was measured.
guard_minimum: 2 participants per condition (smallest size at which a two-sample t statistic is defined); non-finite values and zero pooled variance return None
sizes_note: Source sizes used: 20 observations per cell, two dependent variables (SIM11 Table 1 baseline). Timing: three t tests on 2x20 values, microseconds. SIM11 reports the dependence on the sample size only for optional stopping (Figure 1); for Situation A it states one size (20 per cell) and one correlation (r = .50): the dependence of the error on the sample size is not stated for this situation.
notes: SIM11 simulated normal data with r = .50 between the two measures. That correlation is a property of worlds, not of the brief (the brief may not state it).

passage: Text on Figure 1: a researcher who has already collected 10 (or 20) observations per condition 'and then tests for significance every 1, 5, 10, or 20 per-condition observations' stops once significance is obtained or when each condition reaches 50; starting at 10 and testing after every new per-condition observation finds a significant effect 22% of the time.
faulty: Test the treatment-minus-control mean difference with a two-sample t test (equal variances) after the first 10 observations per condition and then after each additional per-condition observation up to 50 (n = 10, 11, ..., 50, taking the first n observations of each array); the claim is reported as holding if any of these tests has a positive mean difference and p < .05. Parameters from Figure 1: minimum 10 per condition, test after every 1 additional observation, maximum 50 per condition, alpha .05.
fixed: One two-sample t test (equal variances) on all 50 observations per condition, positive mean difference and p < .05.
estimand: Faulty: whether the treatment-control difference reaches significance at any of the sample sizes 10 to 50. Fixed: the treatment-minus-control difference in mean score over all 50 participants per condition (the analysis at the full planned size). The claim says 'on all participants' because the estimand is the analysis at the full size.
guard_minimum: 2 participants per condition; non-finite values and zero pooled variance return None
sizes_note: Source sizes used: maximum 50 per condition, minimum 10 (SIM11 Figure 1 scenario). Timing: 41 t tests on at most 2x50 values per call, computable from cumulative sums in microseconds. The source reports how the error's size depends on the testing frequency and starting size (Figure 1: 22.1% for minimum 10 and tests after every new observation; lower rates for fewer looks and for minimum 20), not on the sample size of a single fixed analysis.
notes: Differs from O2-A in data structure (one outcome, two arms), pipeline step (repeated looks at accumulating data) and sample-size regime (50 per condition, not 20). The brief does not state that rows are in recruitment order; the faulty criterion takes the first n entries of each array.

passage: Section 3.2: gene lists 'were off-by-one due to an indexing error'; 'quantifications from row 98 (probeset 200076_at) of the Gyorffy et al. 2006 table were used instead of those from row 97' (a single-row shift). Section 3.9: 'Poor documentation hid an off-by-one indexing error affecting all genes reported'.
faulty: Locate the signature's rows in the expression table with the membership mask shifted by one row (np.roll of the mask by one position along the probe-set axis), so that each probe set on the list is replaced by the probe set in the adjacent row; compute the per-cell-line average over those rows, then the sensitive-minus-resistant difference and Welch t test (difference at least 0.5 log2 units and p < .01). Parameter: shift of one row, as documented.
fixed: Use the membership mask as given (rows of the probe sets actually on the signature), same averaging, difference at least 0.5 and Welch p < .01.
estimand: Faulty: sensitive-minus-resistant difference in the mean expression of the probe sets one row away from the signature's. Fixed: sensitive-minus-resistant difference in the mean expression of the signature's own probe sets. The claim names the signature because the estimand is its expression difference.
guard_minimum: 2 sensitive and 2 resistant cell lines, and at least 1 probe set on the signature; non-finite values and zero variance return None
sizes_note: Source sizes: NCI-60 panel of 60 cell lines (18 to 30 lines per drug in the signatures read: cisplatin 30, pemetrexed 18); signatures of 45 to 85 probe sets drawn from arrays of 12,558 to 22,283 probe sets. The arrays exceed the 1000-per-axis cap, so 1000 probe sets x 60 cell lines (60 000 values) is used, the largest probe-set axis allowed; cell lines at the NCI-60 size. Timing: one mean over a masked 1000x60 block and a t test, well under a millisecond. The source reports the shift as one row in every case; it does not state how the effect of the shift depends on the sample size or number of features: not stated.
notes: BAG09 also documents reversed sensitive/resistant labels and duplicated samples; this pair uses only the row offset (PB O-3: row or label offsets). The key on_signature is named by what it holds (membership of the published list); possible role-naming reading logged in LOG.md.

passage: Section 2 'Spreadsheet coding error': 'A coding error in the RR working spreadsheet entirely excludes five countries, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, and Denmark, from the analysis.' Footnote: 'RR averaged cells in lines 30 to 44 instead of lines 30 to 49.'
faulty: Compute the mean growth of country-years with debt ratio above 90 and of country-years with debt ratio at or below 90 over the rows of the first 15 of the 20 countries only (drop the first five country rows, i.e. the averaging range stops five lines short), and test that the difference (above minus at-or-below) is at most -2 percentage points. Parameters: 20 countries, 5 rows left out of the averaging range (lines 30-44 of 30-49).
fixed: Compute both means over all country-years of all 20 countries (country-year weighting, as the corrected analysis of HER14 reports), same threshold.
estimand: Faulty: difference in mean real GDP growth between high-debt and other country-years for 15 of the 20 countries. Fixed: the same difference over all 20 countries' country-years. The claim names the 90 percent debt boundary and the growth variable because the estimand is that difference.
guard_minimum: 1 country-year in each debt group (difference of two means is defined from one value each); non-finite values return None
sizes_note: Source sizes used exactly: 20 advanced economies, 1946-2009 (64 years), 1280 country-years; RR reported 96 country-years in the highest category, HER14 corrected 110. HER14 notes the spreadsheet error alone, compounded with the other errors, moved the published mean in the highest debt category by -0.3 percentage points; the dependence on sample size or number of features is not stated. Timing negligible (1280 values).
notes: HER14 also documents selective exclusion of years (Australia 1946-1950, Canada 1946-1950, New Zealand 1946-1949) and country-equal weighting; this pair uses only the spreadsheet range error. The source's arrays have gaps; the brief's arrays are complete because non-finite values trigger an allowed guard that would return None.
